Shouldn't be verified under any circumstances, and was the title that convinced me the label can be bought for the right price.

You can play through the tutorial with zero issues performance-wise, which was enough to convince me it would be fine. The second you enter the real start of the game everything ranks BADLY.

I would only recommend this version of the game if it is on a huge sale.
It is clear that with this release, the ride on nostalgia was the strategy from the start. It runs poorly, with still a lot of bugs to be patched. The game hasn't gotten an update in a year and it seems there is no intention there will be coming one anytime soon.

My game was playing great until this last update we had in July 2025. Then it started to crash every time I went to load my game. I had to restart my game to get it to work and in doing so lost 24 hours of gameplay.

That being said, it's a great remaster. I've been having a blast with it. It plays really well on the Steam Deck. I just wish that update didn't screw up my other game ☠️

Please do not let nostalgia blind you!

This is just a re-skin of an old janky game that I loved, there are more bugs and preforamance issues in this. Which I hoped they would of fixed after launch... but Bethesda, we should of known.

There was deep look into the game, the longer you play, the more it gives issues and frame drops. Which Bethesda has not fixed, but instead porting it to the switch 2.

Game is not worth the price or when on sale, rather play the modded orignal if you has an itch.

No matter, please do not support Bethesda! from now and in the future

I appreciate the graphical update and combat tweaks, believe me.

But if you want proof this was just a blatant cashgrab, be aware that the Dev team for this has went completely silent for about a year now, with no plans unveiled for further optimization or anything.

Bethesda made their money and thats that.

Still has broken quest, it eats memory like no joke, causes crashes and even keeps my PC on when I turn it off. PC runs better with this game not installed at all. How this is allowed on the store or that they have not put out more patches is beyond me...

fun single player game but full of bugs and glitches and crashes like all games these days.

Somehow, this is the same old Oblivion with modern graphics and not much else (they did mix up the leveling system with Skyrim's, but the core of the Oblivion system is still the base, which is great). The same old jank (or charm, to people like me who played this way back) is still very much present in this graphically updated re-release.
Performance-wise, if you don't dick around with Lumen stuff it runs pretty well, but enabling ultra HW RT Lumen brought my framerate down to the high 50s on a 4080 at 1440p. 

Still, this is exactly the game I remembered, with cosmetic changes and not much else. And that's exactly what I wanted. Todd wins again, I guess!
decent enough of a remaster, unplayable mess on top end hardware is not justifiable, extremely poor performance.
Broken and bugged. Very sad, I have to get Google's help to progress basic quests is very frustrating.

This could of been a perfect game if they hadnt abandoned it. The amount of messing around you have to do just to fix the buggy video and gameplay.

Like 217k people bought this game Steam wise from what is can see then after one month tanked to 30,000 and now littl over 1.5k play it daily. pretty terrible. If you work out the price and players thats like 10mil. Yep def a cash grab. Ofc Steam takes their cut.

This is one of the best remasters i have ever played, of a game that was already one of my all-time faves. The visual overhaul is epic to an order of magnitude more than i would have been merely satisfied with, what i would have expected of someone's job to recreate a game in a new engine.

Just flat-out stunning.

It doesn't require very powerful hardware, either. Just look up some benchmarks. My RX 6800 at 3440x1440p does an excellent job with every setting maxed out. High resolution, 5 + year-old card.

This remaster is on par, perhaps even better than Diablo 2 Resurrected's reverence and respect for its own source material.
I guess now that i mention that there is ONE thing missing. Because its built from the ground up in a completely new, seperate engine, there is no ability to switch between old and new graphics, a la D2R.

But ,If you are on the fence, don't be.

Buy this game.

P.S if you choose an archer play style, dont be ashamed of turning the difficulty down from Expert to Journeyman. Expert is really tough with bow and arrows.
This is non stop excitement just like the old version but with way better graphics! Hated nothing.

It's a great remaster of the original. However, as everyone else has said, it's just very poorly optimized. There's no legit reason why this game should run as poorly as it does, or be 120GB for that matter either. With some tweaking, it's still worth it in my opinion.

Do NOT buy this game. It runs fine all the way through the tutorial, but then it completely shits itself. Just enough to make it so you can't refund that damn thing since Steam doesn't let you talk to real people anymore. Stole my money and I just have to live with this. Absolutely disgusting.

I was really enjoying the remastered Oblivion, until it lost my saves!

"None of the master files are loaded" is the message.

200+hours!

The lack of updates and staggering levels of incompetence to introduce a bug that renders the game unplayable the more you play it, the unwillingness to fix the issue in any kind of timely manner or acknowledge the issue at all, it's unacceptable. Don't waste your money.
Oblivion is near and dear to my heart and this remaster preserves most of the reasons why I love the game (and adds achievements!). I do find myself missing the potato faces a lot of the time though.

It’s a great classic. It looks prettier than the original by far but also has some of that classic jank.
Best story line of all the elder scrolls games. it also has the best guild quests of the series.

But 1 year, no updates.
- Runs very poorly (unoptimised)
- Old bugs haven't been fixed and several NEW bugs have been introduced.
It's the same game as the original, with a fresh coat of graphics slapped on it. It's all I ever wanted for the game, and I couldn't be happier.
Yeah I don't think a game that barely manages 30 fps at the lowest possible settings deserves a steam deck verified badge. I wouldn't even say its playable. Unsupported is the term.
An NPC shouting repeatedly "Charge the courtyard, leave NONE of THEM STANDING!" in an empty courtyard and the quest won't progress further. True BETHESDA Experience!
As a kid I never had a good enough pc to run this game. Now with adult money and remastered graphics its a replay for the younger self.

good but not for the reasons it should be.

tldr: play if you have never played oblivion before.
dont buy full price if you have played oblivion before.

so this is just oblivion with modernized graphics and some quality of life changes. it in itself isn't revolutionary. its literally just oblivion. the optimization is really bad. i guess khajiits and argonians look much better. but a game this old at that price point just isnt a great deal. the reason it sold well and is being approved is because it is just a re release of a game that was already an amazing game. if you have never played oblivion before and have a good computer to run this on, then i can say that there is a good chance that you will enjoy the game. if you played oblivion before in the past or can stomach older game graphics and tendancies then just go play the old one if you want to play oblivion. otherwise wait for a sale. this is a really hard sell at its pricepoint. bethesda didnt make a great new game. they just reminded the world that they used to know how to.
Another game abandoned by Bethesda because they want modders to fix their mess of a game

Much like everything Bethesda touches in the last decade or so, it's a cash grab. It's a good game, but only because the original was.
Waiting for the inevitable re-release of the original release in another 10 years.

AS someone who has played the original Oblivion, the remaster is pretty good, with the caveat of some things are improved like overall armor design quality and the ui of the magic system, however I feel like there was a charm toward the original Oblivion the remake kinda lacks? technically it has better graphics and the UI is much better but I still feel like the original Staff of Sheogorath in terms of design looks much better than the remake! overall a good game!
Some of the best storytelling in an rpg I've played and now that it has updated mechanics its one of my favorites

Unplayable after a while, they say they fixed a crash that RUINS the game, but it is still ruining my game every time I try to play. Such a bummer that we are in 2025 and these games are still GARBAGE.

First game I've ever had to refund.

At first glance the game really looks like a new and improved remaster of the original game from 2006, and at first it feels like it too with it's heavier combat, polished textures and simplified UI. But after a while you start to notice the absolutely abysmal performance issues. Exiting the sewers my framerate was anything from 80 to 13 in the blink of an eye, all because I was watching a group of npc's in the distance, AND with graphics set to the absolute lowest they could go (not including resolution, which was 1920x1080). Unfortunately this is not acceptable in this day and age and especially with a prize tag of 55€.

I got my money back, sure. But I was also severely disappointed.

Really great to see them remaster this game, but they really only made it look better and that's it. 20 year old bugged out quests still exist. The more you play the game the more it crashes. At this point 87 hours in it crashes every couple of hours. Also, this remaster has been out a month and we are just now pushing out an update?

I tried sticking to it with all the bugs and crashes, but 22 hours of this non-sense was too much. I finally just raged quit, uninstalled, and will never touch the game. Waste of money. You'd think after 20 years bethesda would fix up all the bugs on a remastered version of oblivion. I'll never buy another bethesda game in the future.

All my game does is crash and fail to load. I have a new PC that exceeds the requirements. Loved playing the original game I just wish this one would function properly. I cannot recommend this game until they fix the performance issues.

A lot of people are complaining about performance but it seems fine to me I tweaked my settings a little and I averaged about 100 fps I’m not sure if they fixed it or not but it seems good to me so far

I totally get that they kept all the glitches from the original Oblivion in this game because of the charm but...did they really have to also keep the part where the game crashes every five seconds...?

Broken game is still broken after all this time, devs stole my money so buyer beware!
Update: Devs still abandoned thsi with brand new day one bugs and crashes unresolved

Same old Oblivion with new visuals. You couldn't ask for more than that except a bug-fix patch. I hope we get one soon. I got murdered by a highwayman that was immune to non-magical and non-charged weapons. I've also noted random stuff like guards will pursue you for miles and shopkeepers don't lose money when they buy stuff.

Be aware, this game is most likely larger than Skyrim. You're going to be playing it forever. Clear your schedule.

And it's hilarious that they troll you with DLC again that has NEW horse armor in it.

In short, it's the Oblivion you remember with some minor gameplay updates and a complete graphic overhaul. At the time of writing, it's currently one of the best looking games out there, but it is terribly unstable and prone to stuttering and crashes. I assume it was released with the assumption the modders will do the rest of the work, even though Bethesda doesn't offer any official mod support.

Edit: They have updated the game and fixed SOME of the crashing issues, however the game is still subject to the typical Bethesda "jank" and is still prone to some stuttering, random crashes, and the game flat out not loading when changing areas. They still need to do some more fixing before I recommend this game.

I just can't bring myself to recommend this game. Oblivion was such a huge part of my childhood so I was super excited to play the remaster but the constant crashing really makes this unplayable. I've had a couple of good runs but the frustration I've had having to troubleshoot/restart the game after every crash outweighs the fun I had playing it, unfortunately.

The most recent crash managed to crash my PC so hard it appears to have removed bluetooth capability (???). Anyway, save yourself the anguish and give this one a miss, folks.

If you have not played Skyrim yet, then play this FIRST. This game is great, but because the originals games dungeons were only made by 1-2 people, the dungeons SUCK. I played the OG Oblivion when I was much younger so it felt amazing back then, however, since I have already experienced Skyrim, I have to say that Skyrim dungeons/caves/even exploring in the open world is much smoother and has more content. I am still giving this a thumbs up because it is overall a great remake.
RIP Sir Patrick Stewart. His intro always gets me ready to slap goblin butt cheeks around like it's 2006. I'm not getting any of the crashing or stuttering people are talking about.

Be aware, VRAM optimization is completly shit,

If you have 8GB VRAM or less you will have a lot of sluttering and perfomance issues, mostly on open world or cities. You can use few mods to improve that, but still, you will have perfomance problems time to time.

Base game is reallly good. I loved it.

DO NOT BUY THIS IF YOU'RE LEFT-HANDED!!! THE DEVS ****** THE KEYBINDS!!! The devs added a hard coded bind to the L key to toggle UI and it is NOT able to be changed. I use PL;' for movement in all PC games and NOW I CANT PLAY THE GAME ANYMORE. Waste of $50. You ruined a game I loved with a crap update

Too many bugs that are new to this version that was slapped together by Virtuos that are game breaking and play style inhibiting. With over a month of radio science on game corrupting bugs it is fun but a massive disappointment. Also paint brushes don't float anymore so there goes hours of fun right away.

I might need to give it more time, but I just don't get it.

It doesn't feel like it has any depth, nor does the "charm" do anything for me. The voice acting and the towns are charming to some, but to me having 1 in 2 characters has subpar voice acting, and the reasonably sized towns (For the time) lacking any real quests just irritates me. Having every NPC in these towns and cities being named lead me to believe that they were all important in some way, but instead it left me thinking that the settlements I was in were much smaller than they actually were. God not to mention the dungeons, christ almighty. Talk about the most samey, uninteresting, repetitive portion in any game and make it a core aspect of this game. Three dungeon clears in and I'm already considering skipping the rest. Maybe I'm a Fallout tourist, maybe I take my games too serious and expect high quality all the time, maybe the remaster is straight up not good, but with all the praise I hear about this game and the amount of expectations I had leading into this...

This is your GOAT?

The game looks pretty nice, but i dont like the DLSS implementation as i feel the graphics gets smudged. I almost need to squint to see stuff clearly. But it has clear performance difficulties on different places. My game runs fine, 60-70fps no DLSS, no RT, high to Ultra on 2k (4080 SUPER, i7 10700k, 64gb, SSD) but when i got to Kvatch i noticed heavy frame drops, down to 20 and maxing on 40fps. This is clearly a Unreal Engine problem and a big dissapointment for me when i learned that.

Other than that, the game looks way nicer than the original. It feels equal or better than the original. The menu is more intuitive and the mechanics have been improved.

Played 120 hours no issue, normal bugs nothing crazy. Suddenly just decides it's going to swap back and forth between keyboard/mouse and controller, normally when I have this issue I just switch to keyboard and mouse and rebind the keys to my liking. Except the game won't let you rebind any of the keys even though there's a dedicated menu for it. Can't find a fix for it on steam or reddit that doesn't involve rewriting code or modding the game. My disappointment is immeasurable
Really fun game, recommend to anyone who likes bethesda games like Skyrim or games with a similar vibe.
